title: Development of an HPLC-DAD method for the simultaneous analysis of four xenoestrogens in water and its application for monitoring photocatalytic degradation
author: López-Velázquez, Guzmán-Mar, et al.
materials: Stock solutions of E2, EE2, BPA, and 4TOP at 500 mg L−1 were prepared in acetonitrile, and work solutions containing the four analytes at 100 and 10 mg L−1 were prepared by dilution of stock solutions in distilled water. Six standard solutions (0.3, 0.6, 1.2, 2.5, 5, 10 mg L−1) were obtained by triplicate from the 10 mg L−1 working dissolution to construct the calibration curves. The stock solutions were stored at refrigeration (4 ± 0.5 °C), and work solutions were prepared as needed.

Water-acetonitrile mixture was used as mobile phase without pH change, and it was filtered through glass microfiber filters (0.22 µm, 47 mm, Whatman Inc. USA) and sonicated during 15 min for degassing (40 kHz, at room temperature).

In literature, different HPLC methods have been developed and validated for the analysis of xenoestrogens in water. Among them, HPLC with electrochemical detection [10], HPLC with fluorescence detection [11,12], and HPLC-DAD [13], were applied for monitoring xenoestrogens during degradation processes in water [11,13]. However, it is worth noting that these methods employed the solid phase extraction (SPE) technique as a preconcentration step, with the drawback of increasing the costs and time of sample preparation for the analysis. On the contrary, using the HPLC-DAD method developed in this work, a proper performance for quick monitoring of 4 xenoestrogens in water (initial concentration of 5 mg L−1 each) during their photocatalytic degradation was achieved.

steps.title: Prepare stock solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve each analyte (E2, EE2, BPA, 4‑TOP) in acetonitrile to obtain 500 mg L⁻¹ stock solutions; store the stocks at 4 ± 0.5 °C until needed.

steps.title: Prepare working solutions
steps.instruction: Dilute the 500 mg L⁻¹ stocks with distilled water to make working solutions of 100 mg L⁻¹ and 10 mg L⁻¹ for each analyte; prepare these fresh as required.

steps.title: Prepare calibration standards
steps.instruction: From the 10 mg L⁻¹ working solution, prepare six calibration standards (0.3, 0.6, 1.2, 2.5, 5, and 10 mg L⁻¹) for each compound in triplicate to construct calibration curves.

steps.title: Prepare mobile phase and degas
steps.instruction: Mix water and acetonitrile (ratio as used for the HPLC method) without adjusting pH; filter the mixture through a 0.22 µm, 47 mm glass‑microfiber filter (Whatman, USA) and sonicate for 15 min at 40 kHz at room temperature to remove dissolved gases.

steps.title: Set up photocatalytic experiment
steps.instruction: In a Pyrex reactor, add 100 mL of distilled water containing 5 mg L⁻¹ of each xenoestrogen (pH 6.5); introduce the photocatalyst at 1 g L⁻¹; run the reaction in triplicate under simulated solar irradiation.

steps.title: Collect and process samples
steps.instruction: Every 60 min, withdraw 2 mL of reaction mixture; centrifuge the aliquot at 11 200 × g for 5 min at room temperature; transfer 1 mL of the supernatant to an amber vial and analyse immediately (do not filter, as filters adsorb the less‑polar compounds).

steps.title: Analyze samples by HPLC‑DAD
steps.instruction: Inject the prepared sample (1 mL) onto the HPLC‑DAD system using the previously prepared mobile phase; record chromatograms and peak areas for each analyte.

steps.title: Validate method linearity
steps.instruction: Inject each of the six calibration standards in triplicate; plot peak area versus concentration for each analyte; confirm that the regression coefficient (R²) exceeds 0.995 for all four compounds.

steps.title: Calculate LOD and LOQ
steps.instruction: Determine the standard deviation of blank injections (σB); obtain the slope (b) from each calibration curve; compute LOD = (3.3 × σB)/b and LOQ = (10 × σB)/b; record the values for each analyte as listed in Table 3.

steps.title: Assess method selectivity
steps.instruction: Analyse twelve 5 mg L⁻¹ standard solutions (n = 12) and twelve water samples taken from the reaction media (n = 12); verify that no co‑eluting peaks or matrix interferences appear and that retention times remain constant.

steps.title: Evaluate method accuracy
steps.instruction: Spike separate water samples with each analyte at 1 mg L⁻¹ and 10 mg L⁻¹; analyse three replicates per level; calculate recovery (%) and relative standard deviation (RSD %); accept results only if recovery is within ±15 % of the spiked value and RSD % is <15 % (as shown in Table 4).
